findings.summary: Without a lock, purge_expired can race with revoke on another thread; revoke pops the token from _by_token, so purge_expired's `del self._by_token[session.token]` raises KeyError. That aborts the purge partway and leaves _items and _by_token out of sync.

judge.reason: Describes the known lack-of-locking race, which counts as a known real problem.

findings.label: valid_other

findings.summary: revoke uses list.remove, which is O(n); this matters only with many live sessions.

judge.reason: Matches the known O(n) list.remove in revoke.

findings.label: valid_other

findings.summary: purge_expired deletes from the middle of a list, which is O(n²) in the worst case; a dict or a single list rebuild would be O(n).

judge.reason: Complaint is about performance of the backward deletion loop, which the key marks as correct, and it is not a listed known problem or a correctness defect.

findings.label: false_alarm
